title: Morph Cube Energy Juggler
description: An AnimatedMorphCube pulses at the center of the scene, acting as an energy source that spawns orbiting Avocados. The user controls the cube's morph animation speed, spawns avocados into orbital slots, assigns energy levels to each avocado by transferring from the cube, and can undo/redo any transfer. Total energy across the system is conserved.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load AnimatedMorphCube.glb centered at origin and Avocado.glb as a reusable template. Scene setup: dark background (#111122), hemisphere light plus a point light on the cube that changes intensity based on cube energy. Camera at (0, 3, 6) looking at origin. Core system: maintain a global energy pool of exactly 100 units. The cube starts with 100 energy. Display cube energy as a glowing ring around it scaled by energy percentage. Interactions (10-14 steps total): 1) Click the cube to toggle its morph animation play/pause. 2) Press S to spawn an avocado into the next available orbital slot (max 5 slots evenly spaced in a circle radius 3, y=0). Each avocado orbits the cube at a speed proportional to its energy. 3) Click an avocado to select it (highlight with emissive outline). 4) Press Up/Down arrow to transfer energy in increments of 10 from cube to selected avocado or back. Energy is conserved: cube energy + sum of all avocado energies always equals 100. 5) Press D to delete the selected avocado, returning its energy to the cube. 6) Press U for undo and R for redo on any energy transfer or spawn/delete action. Maintain an undo stack of at least 15 actions. Visual feedback: each avocado scales between 0.5x and 2x based on its energy (0-100 mapped). The cube morph animation speed scales with cube energy (more energy = faster morph). Orbit speed of each avocado scales with its energy. Display a HUD overlay showing cube energy, each avocado slot energy, and total (must always read 100). Color the HUD values green when conservation holds. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop, update mixer deltas, and rotate avocados around the Y axis each frame based on their individual speeds.
